newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-RAIN MAY DISRUPT SECOND GAME OF INDEPENDENCE CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN MAY DISRUPT SECOND GAME OF INDEPENDENCE CUP FINAL.

text.p: Thunderstorms may disrupt the second match of the best-of-three final between Pakistan and Sri Lanka in the Independence Cup tournament, weather forecasters said on Monday.
The second final is scheduled for Tuesday in Calcutta. Sri Lanka won the first final played on Saturday in the northern town of Mohali.
A rainstorm lashed Calcutta on Monday, preventing both teams from holding practice sessions until late evening.
"There is a possibility of light rains with thundershowers and squally winds (on Tuesday)," R. Goldar, director of the meteorological office in Calcutta, told Reuters.
The Sri Lankans, who crushed the Pakistanis by 115 runs on Saturday, are confident of lifting the Cup.

"We came here to win and not lose," Sri Lankan captain Arjuna Ranatunga told reporters, adding that he hoped his strike opening bowler Chaminda Vass would recover from a back injury and play on Tuesday.
Injury-plagued Pakistan will not play their middle-order batsman Inzamam-ul-Haq, who hurt his palm during Saturday's match.
Pakistan captain Rameez Raja said Inzamam-ul-Haq would be replaced by Mohammed Wasim, another middle-order batsman.
He said the Pakistan team were working on a strategy to contain Sri Lanka's explosive opener Sanath Jayasuriya.
"We will have to get Jayasuriya out in the first two overs," Raja said.
